First, we apply the addition principle, adding $1$ to both sides:

\begin{align} 8 &> -3y -1 \\[5pt] 8+1&> -3y -1+1 \\[5pt] 9 &> -3y + 0 \\[5pt] 9 &> -3y \end{align}

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-3.$

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign:

\begin{align} \require{cancel} 9 \,\,&{\color{blue}> \,\,} {-3y} \\[5pt] \dfrac{9}{-3} \,&{\color{red}< \,\,} \dfrac {-3y}{-3} \\[5pt] -3 \,&{\color{red}< \,\,} \dfrac {\cancel{-3}y}{\cancel{-3}} \\[5pt] -3 \,&{\color{red}< \,\,} y \end{align}

Finally, let's swap the left and right-hand sides so that the variable is on the left-hand side. Remember, we also need to flip the inequality.

\[ y > -3 \]

Therefore, the solution is $y > -3.$

question.text: The solution to the inequality $-4x + 5 < -7$ is $x$
question.explanation:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $5$ from both sides: \begin{align*} -4x + 5 &< -7 \\[5pt] -4x + 5-5 &< -7-5 \\[5pt] -4x + 0 &< -12 \\[5pt] -4x &< -12 \end{align*}

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-4.$

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign: \begin{align*} \require{cancel} -4x \,\,&{\color{blue}< \,\,} -12 \\[5pt] \dfrac{-4x}{-4} \,&{\color{red}> \,\,} \dfrac{-12}{-4} \\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{-4}x}{\cancel{-4}} \,&{\color{red}> \,\,} {3} \\[5pt] x \,\,&{\color{red}> \,} {3} \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $x \bbox[4pt,Gainsboro]{\color{red} > } \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 3 }.$

question.text: The solution to the inequality $-2x + 10 \ge 4$ is $x$
question.explanation:
First, we apply the addition principle, subtracting $10$ from both sides: \begin{align*} -2x + 10 &\ge 4 \\[5pt] -2x + 10 - 10 &\ge 4 - 10 \\[5pt] -2x + 0 &\ge -6 \\[5pt] -2x &\ge -6 \end{align*}

Then, we apply the multiplication principle, dividing both sides by $-2.$

Remember, when multiplying or dividing an inequality by a negative number, we need to flip the inequality sign: \begin{align*} \require{cancel} -2x \,\,&{\color{blue}\ge\,\,} -6 \\[5pt] \dfrac{-2x}{-2} \,&{\color{red}\le\,\,} \dfrac{-6}{-2} \\[5pt] \dfrac{\cancel{-2}x}{\cancel{-2}} \,&{\color{red}\le\,\,} {3} \\[5pt] x \,\,&{\color{red}\le\,} {3} \end{align*}

Therefore, the solution is $x\bbox[4pt,Gainsboro]{\color{red} \le } \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 3 }.$
